effect_mechanism: Putting tree cover back on cleared or degraded land rebuilds the structure that forest species need, and then lets dispersers do the rest. Measured against degraded ecosystems across 221 study landscapes worldwide, forest restoration enhanced biodiversity by 15-84% and vegetation structure by 36-77% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1]. How the cover is re-established changes the result: natural regeneration surpassed active restoration for plants, birds and invertebrates, with restoration success 34 to 56% higher after controlling for forest cover, precipitation and time [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1]. Recovery is a function of time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], and the clock is slow — a secondary Atlantic forest was estimated to need 65 years, with a range of 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. What accelerates it is anything that brings seed in or keeps grazing out: beneath framework-species plantings, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]; artificial perches brought native zoochoric regeneration that was absent from the planted rings [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2]; and Senegalese exclosures carried 27 woody species after a year against 51 in the 5- and 12-year enclosures, more than 52% higher richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. Practitioners implementing these technologies in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, India, Niger and Turkmenistan record plant, animal and habitat diversity rising as cover returns and protection holds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The other route is keeping the forest that exists, since the governance instruments that retain cover also hold the habitat: GEF sustainable forest management sites lost about 0.27% less forest each year than matched areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], payments improved forest cover and reduced deforestation in pooled analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2], and participatory management is credited with regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2].

Natural regeneration and the cross-practice meta-analysis hold the strongest results [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]. Assisted regeneration and forest protection and community management read moderate: the assisted-regeneration evidence is perch and practitioner results, and much of the protection evidence is forest cover and governance with mixed outcomes [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1]. effect_mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for habitat. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) compared with areas without payments [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas, which limits what they deliver for biodiversity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. Most units measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy for biodiversity, not species. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, while the World Bank units are evaluation narratives that cover only projects that monitored outcomes; all concern keeping or managing existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration planting.

effect_mechanism: In these upper-middle-income settings the evidence is about succession on land that has been cleared or degraded, and about what speeds it up. Tree species richness rose as a function of time since disturbance across an Atlantic rainforest chronosequence [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], with a forest estimated to need 65 years, range 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. Assisted recruitment shortens the wait: beneath framework-species plantings in Thai dry forest, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and artificial perches produced native zoochoric regenerants that were absent from planted rings, so bringing in dispersers mattered more than the planting itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1]. On Turkmen barkhan sands the revegetated area is recorded as providing habitat for 25-27 species of plants and animals, with plant and animal diversity rated as increasing [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. Holding the cover is the companion mechanism: under community forest management in the Sierra Norte de Puebla, forest cover did not decline after the handover but increased by 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1].
conditionality: The direction is consistent, but the base is thin and soft: chronosequences and site studies, a set of compiler ratings, and a forest-cover change read from land-use maps as a proxy for habitat rather than a count of species [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Where a project was independently evaluated the result was less flattering — biodiversity is hard to assess, the management-effectiveness tool used was not a suitable proxy, and there was no clear-cut evidence that a Vietnamese special-use forest project had a positive impact [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]. Time is the binding condition: the Atlantic-forest estimate spans decades to well over a century before the assemblage approaches the composition of a mature forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2], so nothing here promises a measurable result inside a project cycle. Two reading rules apply. The gains are measured against the degraded or cleared starting point, not against intact forest, and a young stand holding less than old-growth is incomplete recovery rather than loss. And the perch and framework-species findings are about assisting dispersal into a restoration site [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]: they presuppose a seed source within reach, which is a siting condition a scan can test and a restoration in a cleared landscape may fail.

effect_mechanism: Both directions are reported. On the gain side, planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand thirty-six tree seedling species recruited naturally, 25 of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and WOCAT compilers rate dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan as raising plant, habitat and animal diversity, citing snakes, lizards and turtles [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. On the loss side, a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, tree planting can reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]. A systematic review of nature-based solutions for food security adds that afforestation of natural grassland, which it names as agroforestry done incorrectly, can actually diminish the natural biodiversity of the study area [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguy24n_3]. That is a second-hand expert statement: the review repeats it from a source it cites, in conditional wording, and reports no measurement of its own behind it.
conditionality: What separates the gain side from the loss side is what the land would do without planting. The cautions apply where forests can regenerate naturally [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1] and where the land is natural grassland that afforestation would replace [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguy24n_3]; the gains are on bare dunes and degraded tropical land with no unplanted control [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity]. The actionable reading is a siting and design choice: planting looks favourable where nothing would regenerate otherwise, and risky where natural regeneration is possible or where the existing open ecosystem has its own biodiversity, unless the species and management provide habitat. Both sides remain thin. The loss side is a review sentence and a cited caution repeated by a food-security review, neither of them a measured comparison; the gain side is compiler ratings and a case study without a control. Weigh the new caution as a remark carried from elsewhere, not as fresh evidence of loss. The plantation-versus-natural-regeneration comparisons that used to weigh on the loss side have moved to the plantation family's biodiversity row.

effect_mechanism: Natural regeneration rebuilds biodiversity as secondary forest develops. Across tropical chronosequences species richness recovers fastest and composition slowest, with richness after 20 years at 78% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2]; tree species richness in Brazil's Atlantic Forest rises with time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]; and in the western Andes of Colombia bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest came to resemble old growth [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]. A pantropical meta-analysis finds natural regeneration outperforms active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], an Ethiopian WOCAT compiler rates animal diversity as increased under area closure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity], and in Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness in exclosures rose from 27 species after 1 year to 51 species after 5 and 12 years, an increase of more than 52% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].
conditionality: Recovery of composition and endemism is slow: composition after 20 years was only 33% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1], and in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. effect_mechanism: The units that set the class both point toward loss. The first is an INRAE expert synthesis's own small meta-analysis of species richness in plantations against natural regeneration of the stand after regeneration cutting: -0.24, a very imprecise estimate from a very small number of cases, with an interval that spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. The other is a systematic review of nature-based solutions for food security, which states that plantations of non-native trees, named as agroforestry done incorrectly, can actually diminish the natural biodiversity of the study area [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguy24n_2]. That unit is a second-hand expert statement, not a measurement: the review carries it from a source it cites, in conditional wording ('if done incorrectly ... can'). Further INRAE statements point the same way — plantations generally lead to decreases in biodiversity, or at least to changes in composition at the expense of native species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6], and a cited 40% loss of local species richness in forest plantations relative to uncut control forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2].
conditionality: The negative reading rests on a non-significant estimate whose interval spans zero and on a repeated expert caution; neither is a demonstrated loss measured against the land a plantation replaces. The declines against uncut or near-natural forest are held out of the class because their comparator is reference forest, not the starting point of a restoration project, so they describe a shortfall from a natural baseline rather than a restoration effect [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6]. Even so, every unit in the pool points toward loss and none toward gain. The caution also carries its own condition: it is aimed at plantations of non-native trees and at planting done incorrectly, not at every plantation [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguy24n_2]. The INRAE evidence is temperate and boreal, and the review statement names no setting, so none of this is grounded in the low- and lower-middle-income target. The plantation family is kept out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate plant and animal diversity as increased under protection [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].

In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. effect_mechanism: Across the restoration families taken together, carbon gains are real but uneven between families; they accrue in two pools: biomass as the trees grow, and soil organic carbon after the land-use transition. On biomass, natural regeneration removed 9.1 to 18.8 t CO2 per hectare per year during the first 20 years of growth [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3]. Stock estimates line up with those rates: a 20-year-old secondary natural forest in the moist tropical biome was estimated at 51 t of aboveground carbon per hectare [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch19_1], the median present value of 30-year accumulation from natural regeneration is 60.2 tC per hectare in above- and belowground biomass and soil [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1], and regeneration over 215 Mha could sequester 23.4 Gt of carbon in aboveground biomass over 30 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_williams24_1]. Measured plantings show the accumulation directly: native-species restoration on former pasture held 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 t C per hectare at three, five and seven years [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3], and intervention sites were sequestering approximately 1.33 tons of carbon per hectare per year more than without the project [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. On soils, across 151 transitions to forest the average carbon gain was 0.447% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_1], and practitioners across Niger, India, Tunisia, Bangladesh and Eritrea rate soil organic matter and above-ground biomass as rising under these technologies [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1568_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1330_2010_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C]. Avoided loss carries the rest: keeping existing cover through community management, payments and project support is counted here as retained carbon [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2].

effect_mechanism: A global review finds planted forests and woodlots have the highest CO2 removal rates, 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2/ha/yr during the first 20 years of growth [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1], and plantation reforestation with cyclical harvest accumulates a modelled median of 44.6 tC/ha across aboveground and belowground biomass, soil and harvested wood products [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. Soil carbon also rises: afforestation of cropland raised soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on average and tropical transitions to plantation gained 0.919% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_2], and the compiler for afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland in Uzbekistan reports surface biomass growth of 20 t/hectare/year and soil organic matter up by 20% in the form of fallen leaves [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1533_2011_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1533_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
conditionality: Soil gains are conditional: on pastures (3%) and natural grasslands the change was not significantly different from zero, boreal sites lost 1.5% while other zones gained 7 to 17%, low-clay soils showed no change, heavily disturbed site preparation cut the gain to 4% against 19% with low disturbance, and plantation density made no difference [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_10]; that meta-analysis draws mostly on high-income temperate sites. The planted-forest removal range spans eucalyptus, teak and pine among other species, and the modelled 44.6 tC/ha counts harvested wood products and is a discounted present value [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation results, planted forests, woodlots and plantations under cyclical harvest. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. Plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations, Costa Rican payments for reforestation plantings and modelled plantation profitability, are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

In Guanacaste, Costa Rica, payments for environmental services under the reforestation modality made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract, covered a substantial part of the costs of establishing and maintaining the plantation, and brought family employment and legal security over the property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]; similar Latin American programmes reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Modelled plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area feasible for them [ev_economic_return_busch24_1], and compilers for afforestation in Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns as very positive, the Uzbek compiler noting that unprofitable land would start bringing benefit [ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income].
conditionality: These are production-plantation results: smallholder plantations, commercial plantations under a payment scheme, and modelled plantations with harvest. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], the Costa Rica evidence comes from a high-income setting, and the Uganda compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are compiler ratings or modelled, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_iufro20_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand and, in large studies controlling for socio-economic factors, drove poverty reduction [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]: a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small positive effects of protected areas on local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1], households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2], and across developing countries living within 10 km of protected areas with documented tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1% and of child stunting by 13.4%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas even without tourism [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_food_security_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. Exposure to standing forest feeds children: high forest exposure gives at least 25% greater dietary diversity in sub-Saharan Africa [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4], child dietary diversity rises with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and in Malawi children in communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3], and WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate food self-sufficiency and long-term returns as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_economic_return_wocat_5243_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long].

In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; the GEF forest-management portfolio has a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, local studies found no effect of REDD+ on material well-being, and an analysis in Indonesia found potentially negative effects [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6]; payment programmes have a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3], and payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index in Mexico [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1], where the payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Benefits skew to the better-off: in Nepal poor and low-caste households receive much less while bearing more costs [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]; near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent and lowest-quartile households lost 6 per cent and 10 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; at Bach Ma benefits were shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Livelihood components often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims, and benefit-sharing around Vietnam's special-use forests averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact [ev_household_income_ieg13_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_2]. Protected-area gains depend on tourism: no child growth or wealth gains were found near protected areas without documented tourism [ev_food_security_naidoo19_2], and the forest-diet effect turns significantly negative in richer communities [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_5]. The protected-area, tree-cover and forest-exposure studies measure what living near standing forest provides, not the outcome of a restoration intervention; the Colombian benefit of $411–1,236 per hectare a year is a carbon valuation, not cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3]; and many figures are secondary citations in reviews or World Bank evaluation estimates without a comparison group.

In the protection and community forest management row, the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands, the Afghanistan compiler rates surface runoff decreased, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. The active planting row carries the measured and modelled magnitudes: in the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing, tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year, targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent, and China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1]. Erosion can still worsen under poor management, and this is reported as harm rather than averaged away: particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].
conditionality: Until review, the losses in this row carried as much weight as the gains. What changed that is a unit Pete Steward rejected at review: a cited synthesis statement that plantations without understorey increase the kinetic energy of throughfall and the detachment of soil particles, which he dropped because it had no valid comparator. Without it the loss side rests on the FAO/CIFOR account of plantations stripped of vegetation and litter, which no longer carries as much weight as the gains. The loss statement is cited from a synthesis rather than measured and also states no comparator, and the gain side is a high-income Italian catchment study plus compiler ratings from Uganda. effect_mechanism: This row describes the slope stability that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: landslides begin to increase when roots decay at around three years after forest clearance and susceptibility remains high until around 15 years, rates of mass erosion on steep forested terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after timber harvesting, and in southeast Alaska the area affected by landslides after logging was 5 times greater than in a 100-year period before it [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis likewise notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil a certain amount of mechanical support, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The landslide units are forest-loss contrasts and expert consensus, largely from temperate regions and cited second-hand, so they show what clearing costs rather than measuring the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. The root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by the presence or absence of a well-developed forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. A measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1].
